I am 33 years old. I never went to school, not one day. But I have been in these fields since I was a small boy following my father, so I know every lump of soil in Quzhou. My family has 4.1 mu of land. That is small, so I have to be careful with every yuan I spend.

I divide my land like this: 2.5 mu I do wheat then maize, because that is what everyone around here does. The other 1.6 mu I grow cotton. Last year cotton prices were alright, and my neighbor Lao Wang made money on cotton, so I keep some.

For wheat on the 2.5 mu: I buy the improved wheat seed from the county shop. It is the same kind my cousin used last year and his yield was good. At planting time, I put down one full bag of compound fertilizer per mu — those are the 50 kg bags. Then in the spring, when the wheat turns green, I spread half a bag of white urea per mu, that is 25 kg. My father did this, Lao Wang does this, and last year my wheat was okay. I would rather put a little too much than too little — if I lose the wheat, my family is in trouble. I irrigate three times from my well: before winter, in spring when it shoots up, and when the grain is filling. Water costs electricity, so I do not do more than three. I spray pesticide twice. I rotary till before planting because my neighbor has a small tractor and I pay him a little money to do it fast. I expect about 450 kg per mu.

For maize on that same 2.5 mu after wheat: I plant hybrid maize seed right away after wheat harvest. Everyone uses hybrid now, you cannot even find the old kind anymore. I put down one bag of compound per mu at planting, and then when the maize is knee-high I topdress with half a bag of urea per mu. Maize eats more than wheat if you want full ears. I irrigate twice — once when the tassels come out, that is the important one, and once when the grain fills. If the rains come good, maybe once, but I plan for two. I spray twice for the corn borers and mites. I rotary till quick after wheat harvest. I expect 550 kg per mu. Last year I got 520, so this year I hope for a bit more.

For cotton on the 1.6 mu: I plant improved cotton seed. Cotton stays in the ground a long time and needs a lot of spraying, so I only keep 1.6 mu for it. I put half a bag of compound per mu, and when it flowers I put one handful of urea around each plant — that works out to about 15 kg per mu. I do not put as much on cotton as on grain, because cotton is a gamble and the chemicals already cost too much. I irrigate three times: at planting, at flowering, and when the bolls open. I spray four times, maybe five if the worms are bad — cotton always has bollworms and red spiders. I plough the cotton field deep because my father said cotton likes loose soil. I expect 220 kg per mu of seed cotton.

I do all this because this is what I did last year, and last year I did not lose money. My wife works in a factory in Handan and sends money home, so I can buy the fertilizer, but I still count every yuan. If some salesman tells me to buy a new fertilizer, I tell him to show me Lao Wang's field first. Change is risky. I watch what my neighbors do. If everyone puts one bag per mu, I put one bag per mu.
